bug_semantics: The manage-downloads admin deletion handler accepted attacker-controlled POST fields `file` and `file_name` independently of the integer `file_id`; when `unlinkfile=1`, it concatenated the configured download directory with `file` and passed the result to `unlink()`. Neither the original `trim()` nor the later `sanitize_text_field()` removes `../` segments or proves containment, so an authenticated administrator holding the normal delete nonce could alter the hidden `file` field and delete an arbitrary server file outside the download directory. Deleting a critical file such as wp-config.php can cause denial of service and can enable follow-on site compromise/RCE.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable trust boundary was present in the first public upstream source revision, WordPress Plugin SVN r7446 (2007-01-21): `trunk/downloadmanager/download-manager.php` read `$_POST['file']` and used it in `unlink($file_path.'/'.$file)` rather than deriving the path from the database row selected by `file_id`. Later renames, SVN-to-Git deployment, sanitization, and formatting preserved that mechanism. Git commit d3470a8971d9043438c8aad281cf37d14fefa208 fixed the root cause by accepting only `file_id`, reloading the downloads-table row, and unlinking the stored `$file->file` value.
ai_marker: absent — the canonical BIC is SVN changeset r7446, whose commit metadata is author `GamerZ`, timestamp `2007-01-21 10:26:57`, and exact log message `WP-DownloadManager First Commit`; SVN exposes no separate committer or trailer block, and the revision has no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/bot marker.
evidence: Advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w2w8-j4gc-v26q identifies CVE-2026-2426 as path traversal through the deletion `file` parameter, affecting all versions through 1.69 and fixed in 1.69.1; its first-party fix reference is https://github.com/lesterchan/wp-downloadmanager/commit/d3470a8971d9043438c8aad281cf37d14fefa208.

Fix inspection: `git show --format=fuller --stat --patch d3470a8971d9043438c8aad281cf37d14fefa208` shows the handler deleting the POST-derived `$file = sanitize_text_field($_POST['file'])` and `$file_name` assignments, adding a prepared SELECT by integer `file_id`, and changing `unlink($file_path.$file)` to `unlink($file_path . $file->file)`. The same commit changes the plugin version from 1.69 to 1.69.1 and its message is `Fetch file using file_id again instead of relying/trusting form post file POST param`.

Vulnerable boundary: `git show b8e6bd8d773baa58846cd06e3fcb72f06f7bcf56:wp-downloadmanager.php` identifies the direct fix parent as version 1.69. The WordPress SVN 1.69 source at https://plugins.svn.wordpress.org/wp-downloadmanager/tags/1.69/download-manager.php still reads POST `file`, then calls `unlink($file_path.$file)`; Trac records tag 1.69 at r3364848.

Patched boundary: https://plugins.svn.wordpress.org/wp-downloadmanager/tags/1.69.1/download-manager.php reloads the database row by `file_id` and unlinks `$file->file`; Trac records tag 1.69.1 at r3460449. In the validated Git clone, tag `1.69.1` resolves to 416b9f5459496166c0395f9e055d4c4cf872404a, and `git log d3470a8971d9043438c8aad281cf37d14fefa208^..416b9f5459496166c0395f9e055d4c4cf872404a` shows d3470a8971d9043438c8aad281cf37d14fefa208 as its direct ancestor.

BIC reconstruction: following copies in Trac from tags/1.69/download-manager.php reaches the r22764 `Structure Change` rename; following the predecessor `trunk/downloadmanager/download-manager.php` then reaches r7446. The raw r7446 source at https://plugins.svn.wordpress.org/!svn/bc/7446/wp-downloadmanager/trunk/downloadmanager/download-manager.php contains the vulnerable POST-to-unlink sequence and identifies version 1.00 in its header.

Immediate-parent absence: https://plugins.trac.wordpress.org/browser/wp-downloadmanager/trunk?rev=7445 shows the plugin trunk empty, while https://plugins.trac.wordpress.org/changeset/7446/wp-downloadmanager records four paths added, including `download-manager.php`. Thus the vulnerable deletion mechanism is directly absent from the immediate predecessor tree and first appears in r7446.

Git import excluded as BIC: Git commit 8c862546f81e81283cb2afeea193a6b7ac522b50 (`First commit to wp-downloadmanager`, 2013) adds a snapshot already containing the flaw, and its parent a09241ef80dae7961961ed0bf637cfeaef23cb33 contains only README.md. Because public SVN history proves the same lines in r7446 six years earlier, the Git snapshot is an import, not the causal introducer.

SHA null justification: the smallest public causal BIC is canonical WordPress SVN revision r7446, which has a numeric revision identifier rather than a Git object ID; its immediate predecessor is SVN r7445 for the same reason. Substituting the later Git import's 40-hex SHA would violate the protocol's smallest-real-BIC rule. The fix is in Git and therefore is recorded with its full 40-hex SHA.
reasoning: The vulnerability is not merely weak output sanitization: the deletion action trusted a client-supplied pathname and joined it to a privileged filesystem base. Capability and nonce checks limit exploitation to an authenticated administrator and prevent ordinary CSRF, but they do not constrain a malicious administrator's modified POST body. History must be followed across two provenance transitions. The 2013 Git repository introduction is only a deployment snapshot; WordPress SVN proves the same mechanism in the pre-rename file, and the chain terminates at first-public revision r7446, where the file and vulnerable handler are added while r7445 has an empty plugin trunk. That is the smallest real BIC, so its numeric SVN identity is reported rather than falsely labeling the Git import as the introducer. The mechanism spans version 1.00 through the vulnerable 1.69 tag. Direct fix d3470a8971d9043438c8aad281cf37d14fefa208 changes the data provenance: it discards POST `file`, reloads by `file_id`, uses the stored path, and bumps 1.69 to 1.69.1; the 1.69.1 Git/SVN release includes it. AI attribution is evaluated only on r7446 metadata: human maintainer identity `GamerZ`, a 2007 first-commit message, and no AI/bot/co-author/generated trailer signal. Therefore the vulnerability is NOT_AI.
